name: Stock Asset Readiness Checker
description: Upload an image and auto-check resolution, format, transparency, aspect ratio and size against Adobe Stock, Shutterstock, Freepik or Envato requirements.
body:
🖼️

Drop your image here or click to browse

JPG, PNG or WebP — processed 100% in your browser

Upload an image to see its readiness report.

—Resolution
—Aspect ratio
—File size
—Auto score

Manual checklist
howto: Pick the stock platform you are submitting to from the dropdown.
Upload your image with the dropzone or file picker.
Read the automatic checks — each one shows pass, warning or fail with the exact requirement.
Work through the manual checklist for things only you can verify (logos, faces, watermarks).
Use the summary note to fix any failing check before submitting.
features: Platform presets for Adobe Stock, Shutterstock, Freepik and Envato
Automatic resolution, format, transparency, aspect ratio and size checks
Clear pass / warning / fail status with the specific requirement shown
Manual submission checklist for non-automatable rules
Overall score plus a summary note that lists exactly what to fix

faq.q: Which resolution do the major stock platforms require?
faq.a: Adobe Stock, Shutterstock and Envato accept a 4 megapixel (MP) minimum — Adobe also caps uploads at 45MP and 20MB. Freepik asks for at least 1000px on the longest side. The preset dropdown applies the exact numbers for each platform.

faq.q: Does this tool upload my image anywhere?
faq.a: No. Every check runs locally in your browser using the image's own data. Your file never leaves your device.

faq.q: Why does it warn about transparency?
faq.a: Adobe Stock does not accept transparent-background images unless you have an approved transparent template. If a PNG has an alpha channel and you are submitting a regular photo, convert it to JPEG first.

faq.q: Can this tool guarantee my image will be accepted?
faq.a: No. It only verifies the technical requirements you can measure (dimensions, format, transparency, size) and reminds you of the content rules. Reviewers also judge quality, composition and legal releases.
